item.title: 5 things to keep an eye on in the 49ers-Cowboys Week 10 matchup
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers take on the Dallas Cowboys in their 43rd regular-season meeting. Here are five things to watch for this Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The San Francisco 49ers will be on the road against the Dallas Cowboys for a Week 10 matchup Nov. 15 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.

The Niners enter the contest with the best record in the NFC at 7-1, while the Cowboys, who are struggling to find a consistent groove, are second in the NFC East at 4-5. The 49ers are coming off a 38-17 win against the Las Vegas Raiders behind five turnovers forced by their defense.

San Francisco will gets its first look at veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen in a 49ers uniform following his acquisition in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts just before the NFL trade deadline. Allen helps the Niners' receiving corps that has seen injuries to Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, Ricky Pearsall and De'Zhaun Stribling.

The Cowboys are hoping to get back to .500 and find some sort of rhythm in what's been a disappointing season so far. Dallas is coming off a 27-23 victory against the Colts led by quarterback Dak Prescott, who completed 21-of-34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns. Running back Javonte Williams ran for 101 yards and a touchdown on 20 carries. Receiver CeeDee Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown.

Niners-Cowboys remains one of the most entertaining rivalries in the NFL. They've had 42 regular-season meetings, with San Francisco holding a 22-19-1 all-time edge.

Here's five things to watch for in 49ers vs. Cowboys on Sunday:

49ers secondary vs. Cowboys receivers

The 49ers secondary will have their hands full going up against Lamb and George Pickens.

Health could be a big factor. Both Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and Renardo Green (back) were injured against the Raiders, but 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said they would be game time decisions.

"We'll see. Obviously, the injury report is the injury report, whatever that says," Morris said. "We'll see those guys, if they can get out there, if they can make it, they'll go. They're tough guys. They're very physical. They're very competitive, so we'll give them the best chance and take it all the way to game day to find out if they can go out there and play for us."

Regardless, the matchup with Pickens, Lamb and the Dallas receivers brings excitement to Morris.

"Obviously, CeeDee (Lamb), when you start with him you're talking about a guy that's highly targeted, a bunch of receptions. He's a volume player. He gets the ball a lot," Morris said. "They put the ball in his hand. He's like all those guys, those (Seattle Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba) JSNs, those (Los Angeles Rams WR Puka) Nacuas and all the guys in our division, where they target him a lot and he's heavily targeted."

"Then you’ve got that freak on the other side, Pickens, sometimes on the same side," he added. "He's got freak-like ability. He's a great mover. He's very versatile, can do a bunch of different things. He can shock you in all types of ways down the field, vertical or with catch and run. They're a very, very difficult crew. Very excited about the matchup."

Can 49ers defensive line bring the pressure?

San Francisco has prioritized the defensive line, making sure it's beefed up and deep with able bodies. The Niners brought back former 49ers star DeForest Buckner in a trade with the Colts, adding him to a lineup with Nick Bosa, Keion White, Gracen Halton, Jaden Dugger, Romello Height, CJ West, Osa Odighizuwa and Mykel Williams.

They have depth, now they're focused on bursting into the backfield, getting pressure on the quarterback and being at the scene of the action. San Francisco didn't register any sacks against the Raiders but it brought pressure and that turned into batted balls and turnovers.

“It's really hard when you talk about that. The ball does come out quick, but it's never an excuse. It's really about what happens when the ball comes out quick," Morris said. "Last week we've seen a bunch of screens and a bunch of guys really getting to the football and knocking it down and being in the right spots. ... There was a couple of interceptions out there where you're forcing things early, got a really critical hit by Keion White during that game on a double move that they had, potentially had some hay on, but Keion made a great rush. So, you're really excited about where you can go.

"Obviously, you want the production, particularly for the individual stats and the guys, but really happy where the defense is and when they're playing in the most critical moments," Morris added. "They're being their best when their best is required and that's really all you can ask."

Osa Odighizuwa back in Dallas

Odighizuwa was traded to the 49ers from the Cowboys during the offseason. It was one of the Niners' earlier attempts to beef up their defensive line.

Now, he faces off agaisnt his former team for the first time. It'll be interesting to see what kind of fire that could set under Odighizuwa. Morris is unsure if the defensive lineman has the Cowboys on his mind, but it's worth a watch.

“I don't know. I really didn't talk to him that way. I don't know if guys hold onto those emotional rollercoaster type things," Morris said.

Odighizuwa said in May that joining the Niners gives him a chance to help win a Super Bowl.

"I feel like getting some handcuffs taken off of me a little bit," he said. "(I) definitely want to make the deep playoff run, bro, and get to the dance. I want to get that ring for sure. Being on a team that's been in two of the last (seven Super Bowls) is very hopeful going into the playoffs. I think they made it to the second round of the playoffs with a bunch of guys hurt, you know what I mean?"

George Kittle vs. Cowboys

Tight end George Kittle doesn't care for the Cowboys. He often wears a special, anti-Cowboys T-shirt to commemorate these games.

Just be on the lookout if he wears it again. He said he "potentially" will. Imagine if he scores and reveals it?

49ers' offensive weapons

Wide receiver Jordan Watkins had a big game last week. Expect him to be a target that Brock Purdy looks for more frequently after he put up four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown against the Raiders.

"He's a guy who has blossomed because of that mindset and he continues to get better every week," 49ers offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak said. "It's really cool to see a guy get rewarded for that with plays and making huge plays for us a couple of weeks in a row. I'm very happy for him and he knows as well as anyone, he has to keep doing that to have that sustained success. ... He's helping our team. He's helping us in the running game. He's making plays. It's a big part of what we're doing on offense right now."

Also be on the lookout for Purdy and Allen to establish a connection.

"It's been awesome. Just a true pro. I feel like he understands looking at our plays and our formations and stuff," Purdy said of Allen. "He's been around the block and understands what the routes are and where he needs to be. He's got really good hands and good feet, creates some really good separation from what I've seen this week so far. ... I'm really excited actually come Sunday to play with him."

item.title: 5 Bills to pay close attention to vs. the Jets
item.description: How will Josh Allen follow up a solid performance against the NFL’s best defense?
item.content:encoded:
The Buffalo Bills are Jersey bound, heading to East Rutherford to take on the New York Jets this week. It’s just the second divisional game for the Bills, as they have just their October loss vs. the New England Patriots on their AFC East ledger so far. The Jets, meanwhile, will finish their first go-rounds of AFC East games with Sunday’s matchup.

While New York may be just 2-7 this season, they’ve played a lot of tight games, including two against the New England Patriots and Miami Dolphins. The Patriots defeated the Jets 26-19, while the Dolphins squeaked out a 28-25 victory. Really, the only game the Jets were entirely demolished in came last week, when they lost 35-12 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Can the Jets play the Bills tight this week? Will Buffalo overlook their division rivals and lose the game outright? There’s no question that Buffalo is the better football team, but there’s a reason why they play the games rather than just talking about them. The Bills will need to come out ready to roll in order to maintain their hold on the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

Here are five Bills to watch on Sunday as they try to do just that.
_____________________________________________________________________________

QB Josh Allen

Last week, after a slow start, Allen caught fire in the second half against an outstanding Minnesota Vikings defense. Allen started his night just 7-of-14 for 51 yards and an interception, but from the Bills’ two-minute drive at the end of the first half until the end of the game, he was electric. Allen completed 14 of his next 21 passes for 183 yards and a touchdown, and while those numbers might sound pedestrian, Allen finished his day as just the second quarterback to eclipse 200 yards passing against the Vikings this season. It was the first time anyone had done it since Jordan Love did it for the Green Bay Packers in Week One. Allen isn’t immune from the occasional stinker, and sometimes, those stinkers come against subpar opponents in the immediate aftermath of a big win. OF Buffalo’s three AFC East foes, Allen also has fewer touchdown passes against the Jets (16) than he does against either the Patriots (25) or Dolphins (42) in his career, and he’s thrown 11 interceptions in 15 games against them. I want to see Allen work just as patiently as he did on Monday night, taking what the Jets’ defense gives him while trusting his teammates to do their part. He doesn’t have to play hero ball this week. He just has to be Josh Allen.

RB James Cook III

Part of me is watching Cook because I expect him to have a big game, as he averaged 4.53 yards per rush in seven career games against the Jets. However, part of me is also watching how head coach and offensive play-caller Joe Brady manages his workload. Cook carried 31 times on Monday, and coming into a short week, I wouldn’t be surprised to see more of Ray Davis in the backfield this week. Cook still needs his touches, but I wouldn’t be mad if his snap share were dialed back a bit in the interest of saving him for later in the season. Davis and Ty Johnson, who is a former Jet, should see some more work this week. If Cook can slip some big runs early, it could help Buffalo to build the kind of lead where he’s hopefully wearing a baseball cap in the fourth quarter.

WR DJ Moore

Yeah, we’re going heavy-hitters this week. Moore has looked good since returning from a shoulder injury, but I’m waiting for him to take over a game like he did when he had five catches for 100 yards and a score on opening day. That’s also, perhaps not coincidentally, the only game he’s played this season where he wasn’t banged up in some way. Moore is doing his job, as he has 19 catches fo 285 yards and 2 touchdowns on 32 targets; however, he hasn’t looked like a bona fide No. 1 wideout. Against a struggling Jets squad that has allowed 16 passing touchdowns against just one interception this season, I’d like to see Moore have a bigger day. The Jets rank well in passing yards allowed—they’re No. 4 in passing yards against—but that’s misleading since they’re often trailing and they’re ranked just 26th against the run. A scoring pass from Allen to Moore on the first drive of the game for the Bills would be a nice way to kick off a Sunday.

OLB Michael Hoecht

Maybe it’s unfair to single him out, as Hoecht hasn’t played more than 41% of the defensive snaps in a game this season, and he’s coming off of Achilles surgery last year. However, he’s been mostly pedestrian when he’s been out there, and he just hasn’t had the burst that he showed in limited action last year. Yes, that’s a byproduct of the injury, as he is just past one calendar year since he tore his Achilles in a win over the Chiefs. But, Hoecht has just 15 tackles to show for his work this season, and half a combined sack of Jared Goff in Week Two is his whole pass-rush output so far. He nearly made a cool play last week when he dove and nearly intercepted a spike. Making a play on Geno Smith and bringing the veteran quarterback to the turf would be nice. If Hoecht can find a groove, given how well Greg Rousseau is playing and the strides that T.J. Parker and Bradley Chubb have made as a duo, it would add another layer to Buffalo’s pass rush as they enter a difficult stretch of schedule.

S Amani Hooker

It has to be the new guy, right? Hooker was exactly the kind of addition the Bills needed. He’s a rangy safety who isn’t afraid to hit, and it sure doesn’t hurt that he’s the NFL’s current leader in interceptions, either. Hooker has allowed just a 60.2 quarterback rating when he’s the closest player in coverage. That’s significantly better than Buffalo’s two starting safeties last week, Cole Bishop (90.3 passer rating allowed) and Damar Hamlin (106 passer rating allowed). Even if the Bills ease him into the festivities, it’s going to be nice to have a high-end safety in the back of the defense. Sunday is a good time to try him out, as the Jets rank just 22nd in passing yards on the year. I’m excited to see what No. 22 brings to Buffalo’s ever-improving defense.

item.title: Bears Week 10 Flashbacks: Concannon’s Bombs, Dent’s Dominance, Vasher’s 108 yards
item.description: Hop aboard the Gridiron Time Machine with @iamcogs and take a trip down Week 10 Bears memory lane!
item.content:encoded:
The Bears may be enjoying their bye week, but the Gridiron Time Machine doesn’t need the week off.

Instead of our usual three games, we’re digging a little deeper this week with five memorable Week 10 performances, spanning nearly 60 years of Bears history.

1. 1967, Bears vs. Cardinals: Concannon goes deep, over and over again

November 19, 1967 | Bears win 30-3

The 1967 Bears were sitting at 4-5 when the St. Louis Cardinals came to Wrigley Field for Week 10.

What followed was one of the more explosive passing performances of the era.

Jack Concannon completed only 11 passes, but those completions went for an incredible 336 yards and three touchdowns. Dick Gordon was responsible for most of the damage, catching four passes for 179 yards and two scores.

The touchdowns were not exactly short ones either.

Concannon connected with Gordon for a 93-yard touchdown early in the second quarter, then found Bob Jones for another 51-yard score. Before halftime arrived, Gordon struck again from 67 yards out.

Three touchdown passes. All three from more than 50 yards away.

Meanwhile, the Bears defense made sure St. Louis never had much of an opportunity to respond.

Chicago intercepted Cardinals quarterbacks seven times, including five picks from Jim Hart alone, while forcing nine turnovers overall. The Cardinals finished with only 230 total yards and never reached the end zone.

Chicago cruised to a 30-3 victory behind 461 yards of offense.

For a franchise that has not exactly been known for explosive passing attacks, Concannon throwing three touchdown passes of 51 yards or longer feels almost out of place in Bears history.

Almost.

2. 1979, Bears vs. Lions: Everybody gets involved

November 4, 1979 | Bears win 35-7

The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1979 season sitting at 4-5 and desperately trying to remain in the playoff picture.

Detroit turned out to be a pretty good opponent for getting things moving in the right direction.

Walter Payton once again carried the offense, rushing for 113 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries while adding another 53 yards as a receiver. Mike Phipps threw for just 136 yards, but Chicago didn’t need much through the air.

The fun really started in the third quarter.

With Chicago leading 14-7, Steve Schubert returned a punt 77 yards for a touchdown. Not long afterward, Terry Schmidt intercepted Lions quarterback Jeff Komlo and returned it 20 yards for another score.

Suddenly, a seven-point game had become a 28-7 Bears lead.

Payton added his second touchdown in the fourth quarter to finish off a 35-7 victory.

Chicago did not commit a turnover while forcing five from Detroit, and Payton finished with 166 yards from scrimmage. The win moved the Bears back to .500 at 5-5 and became part of a late-season push that eventually carried Chicago into the playoffs.

The recipe probably sounds familiar.

Give the ball to Walter Payton, let the defense create mistakes, and sneak in a special teams touchdown while you’re at it.

Very Bears.

3. 1984, Bears vs. Raiders: Richard Dent wrecks the defending champs

November 4, 1984 | Bears win 17-6

One year before the 1985 Bears defense became immortal, Chicago was already showing the rest of the NFL what was coming.

The defending Super Bowl champion Los Angeles Raiders arrived at Soldier Field in Week 10 with a 7-2 record.

They left having scored zero touchdowns.

Walter Payton handled the offensive workload, rushing 27 times for 111 yards and scoring twice in the first half. His touchdown runs of 18 and eight yards gave Chicago a 14-0 advantage before the defense took care of everything else.

And Richard Dent was everywhere.

Dent recorded 4.5 sacks, which remains the Bears’ single-game franchise record. Chicago sacked Raiders quarterbacks nine times overall, forced five turnovers and held Los Angeles to just 181 total yards.

The Raiders managed only two field goals in a 17-6 Bears victory. It was the first time the defending champions had been held without a touchdown in more than three years.

The win moved Chicago to 7-3 and gave the Bears another indication that Buddy Ryan’s defense was developing into something special.

We know what happened one year later.

But before the Super Bowl Shuffle, the playoff shutouts and the legend of the 1985 defense, Richard Dent and company were already making Sundays miserable for opposing quarterbacks.

The defending Super Bowl champions just happened to get an early preview.

4. 1990, Bears vs. Falcons: Vestee Jackson shuts the door

November 11, 1990 | Bears win 30-24

The Bears entered Week 10 of the 1990 season as one of the hottest teams in football.

Atlanta came to Soldier Field and nearly spoiled the afternoon.

After falling behind 3-0, Chicago scored 24 unanswered points behind touchdowns from Neal Anderson, Wendell Davis and Brad Muster. Jim Harbaugh connected with Davis for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter, and the Bears carried a 24-3 advantage into the second half.

Then things got uncomfortable.

Atlanta scored two unanswered touchdowns to cut the lead to 24-17, and what had looked like a comfortable afternoon suddenly became a one-score game.

Fortunately, Chris Miller threw one pass too many.

Vestee Jackson jumped the route and returned the interception 45 yards for a touchdown, pushing the lead back to 30-17 with just over a minute remaining. Atlanta scored once more, but Chicago held on for a 30-24 victory.

Miller threw for 239 yards and two touchdowns, but the Bears intercepted him four times. Wendell Davis led Chicago offensively with five catches for 105 yards and a score, while Harbaugh added 195 passing yards and another 47 on the ground.

The victory improved Chicago to 8-1 and extended its winning streak to five games.

Sometimes the defense dominates from start to finish.

Other times it waits until things get interesting before reminding everyone who is in charge.

5. 2005, Bears vs. 49ers: Nathan Vasher goes 108 yards

November 13, 2005 | Bears win 17-9

If you remember anything about the Bears’ 2005 Week 10 win over San Francisco, it probably isn’t the offense.

That’s because there wasn’t much of one.

Chicago quarterback Kyle Orton threw for only 67 yards. San Francisco quarterback Cody Pickett somehow managed just one completion for 28 yards.

The real star was the wind.

With gusts approaching 50 miles per hour at Soldier Field, 49ers kicker Joe Nedney attempted a 52-yard field goal on the final play of the first half.

The kick fell short.

Nathan Vasher was waiting.

Vasher caught the ball deep in the end zone, briefly hesitated, then took off. He reversed field, found a convoy of blockers and raced all the way to the opposite end zone for a 108-yard touchdown.

At the time, it was the longest play in NFL history.

The return gave Chicago a 7-3 halftime lead in a game where points were extremely difficult to find. Adrian Peterson later rushed for a seven-yard touchdown and finished with 120 yards on 24 carries, while Robbie Gould added a fourth-quarter field goal.

The Bears held on for a 17-9 victory, their fifth straight win, improving to 6-3 while maintaining control of the NFC North.

One year later, Devin Hester would return another missed field goal exactly 108 yards against the Giants.

Apparently 108-yard missed field goal returns were just something Bears defensive backs did for a while.

Gary Baugher Jr. is a second year contributor to WCG, bringing football insight backed by over 16 years of experience in organized football and more than 30 years as a passionate fan of the game. You can follow him on Twitter at @iamcogs.

item.title: Big Blue View mailbag: Kickoff rule, Rasul Douglas interception, more
item.description: The mail’s here! The fallout from Thursday’s loss is, of course, a big topic.
item.content:encoded:
Lou Catalano asks: Could you please explain the rule concerning kickoffs going out of bounds? In the Giants/Washington game, the ball bounced in bounds, the returner stepped out of bounds, then caught the ball while his knee was touching the ground in bounds. What ever happpened to the old John Madden maxim that one knee equals two feet?

Ed says: Lou, you weren’t the only confused by this. The rulebook says:

“A ball that is in player possession is out of bounds when the runner is out of bounds.”

On kickoffs, this is a bit of a loophole. Credit Luke McCaffrey of the Commanders for knowing the rule and making a great play. If you plant your feet out of bounds, then touch a ball that is inbounds, it makes the ball considered to be out of bounds. That creates a kickoff out of bounds and puts the ball at the 40-yard line.

I have seen this happen a couple of times. I have also seen players mess this up by either catching the ball and stepping out of bounds, or by picking the ball up inbounds right near the sideline and trying to return it.

David Silver asks: I’m trying to make sense out of the last throw JJ McCarthy made to Nabers that was intercepted. It looks like McCarthy hung the ball up based on the trajectory. It also gave Nabers plenty of time to get it sighted. Douglas comes from behind to high point Nabers, but it also looked like he hit Nabers early. But that is a 50/50 ball Nabers wants. My question is, bad throw, bad catch attempt, great defensive play, or pass interference?

Ed says: David, sometimes you just have to give the other guy credit. I have watched this play a bunch of times, and I listened to Nabers and John Harbaugh talk about it on Friday.

Washington sent a zero blitz, rushing more players than the Giants could block and forcing J.J. McCarthy to make a split-second decision. His decision was to give the Giants’ best receiver a chance to make a play. Right decision? Wrong decision? Harbaugh just said it was the decision that McCarthy made. Douglas didn’t interfere with Nabers. Nabers said he was focused on tracking the ball and knew there was a defender in the area, but didn’t know where. Douglas did not interfere with Nabers. He just ended up making a play.

The Giants have won a couple of games like that this season. The other guys get paid, too.

Raymond Dansereau asks: How much better are the Giants really than last year? Last year they had a tough schedule and close losses; this year, they’re playing a weak schedule and really not always looking great. Defense seems better, but is this a 10-7 playoffs team that gets beaten badly in the first round? Or, does this look like sustainable improvement? Or too soon to say?

Ed says: Raymond, I can’t go position-by-position or player-by-player in a mailbag response. I think the real answer is that the Giants are better simply because they have John Harbaugh and they are coached better. It doesn’t hurt that this team has Arvell Reese, either.

The Giants are winning close games, which they couldn’t do last year. A lot of that is coaching, whether it is in-game decisions or just preparing players well enough that they believe they are supposed to make plays and win close games.

If it is a 9-7-1 playoff team that gets bounced in the first round, what’s wrong with that? The Giants won seven games combined the past two seasons — a playoff berth would be a fantastic accomplishment. Sustainable improvement? The NFL is such a week-to-week and year-to-year league that is impossible to say. As long as Harbaugh is the coach, though, the Giants have a chance to be relevant. That is a massive improvement.

Matt Smith asks: We’ve had four failures in a row at the head coach position. They are bookended by two Hall of Fame coaches. My question is, seeing how far the gap is between Daboll and Harbaugh, do you find it surprising how long we waited to move on from him? It seems more and more apparent to me that we had talent that we could’ve done with if we had a professional head coach with standards. The red flags were always there.

Ed says: Matt, I’m not at all surprised that the Giants waited as long as they did to move on from Brian Daboll. look at the Giants’ track record:

  • Ben McAdoo lasted less than two full seasons.
  • Pat Shurmur was fired after two seasons.
  • Joe Judge was fired (well, he kinda fired himself) after two seasons.

You cannot get ahead when you have to keep blowing things up and starting over every two years. That means an entire new coaching staff, gutting most of the roster, and starting over. You can never institute a real philosophy or build anything that way.

John Mara knew it, and he said several times that he knew he needed to be more patient than he had been.

Daboll had a shockingly good first season and won Coach of the Year. The Giants could have justified firing him and GM Joe Schoen after a 3-14 2024 season, but chose not to.

Mike Vrabel got hired by New England that offseason. Zero chance he was picking the Giants over the Patriots, the team he played for an an organization he loves. Ben Johnson got hired by the Bears. No chance he was picking the Giants over the Bears, who already had Caleb Williams in place. Liam Coen got hired by the Jaguars, but nobody knew that would work out as well as it had.

It was really the 2025 season when it became clear that the coaching staff wasn’t maximizing the talent of the players.

Adam Singer asks: During the game against the Eagles, it looked like some of the players had a diagonal line through the word “GIANTS” on their helmets while others did not. What was going on there?

Ed says: Adam, the word ‘GIANTS’ was underlined. I think what you saw was the chinstrip, which buckles on the side of the helmet, protruding over the lettering on some of the helmets.

Ronald Lukoff asks: I usually do not disagree with a lot of your comments but I do take exception to your thoughts about the Giants making a blockbuster trade today (this is written Tuesday morning). I have been a Giant fan since 1956. I have seen a lot of success and a lot of failure. This team is made up of a lot of draft picks and I really do not want to give up future draft choices for a player that can give us a division title. This team has only played one team with a record above .500. Do you really think that one player is worth losing draft capital? If I thought one player could get us to the Super Bowl, I might feel differently. Do you think JJ is the answer at QB. He was great first 5 quarters, not so much last game. but a quarterback needy ream just traded him away, so I am hesitant to put all my faith in him and believe me, I hope I’m wrong. I feel like we are at least a year away from potentially going to the Super Bowl and while I would love to win the division, I just don’t think giving up draft choices is the best way to build a championship team. You’re feelings?

Ed says: Ronald, it’s moot at this point since the trade deadline has come and gone. I want to clarify this, anyway.

I wrote earlier in the week that the Giants should try to capitalize on the opportunity they have in the NFC East. You don’t know if or when that opportunity will come again.

They did try to do that. They were very aggressive. They were also careful. I said earlier in the week there was a price they should not go to — meaning they should not go above the second-round pick they had offered the Colts for Jonathan Taylor. They — rightly — refused to do that.

I said all along the end game is not winning the division this year and then going back to being a third- or fourth-place team for fove years after that. The end game is to be a championship contender on a consistent basis. You have to protect your future to do that.

Myles Garrett is coming off a dominating three-sack performance in his return to the Rams’ lineup.

Here’s a scary thought:

“Not a 100 [%],” he told reporters Friday when asked to put a percentage-gauge on how he felt in last Sunday’s victory over the Washington Commanders. “I can’t go that far. We’re not a 100 but we’re trying to make our way there.”

Garrett, who sat out seven games while recovering from left knee surgery, is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals. But he is expected to play as the Rams attempt to extend their winning streak to four games.

The two-time NFL defensive player of the year’s influence on the team extends beyond the field.

In the locker room, the 10th-year pro is the top-rated player in a player-organized, no-contact shadow-boxing league designed to instill competition and camaraderie.

Garrett, who spent his first nine seasons with the Cleveland Browns, said he didn’t bring the competition with him, “but I will say I was the top dog where I left and top dog now, so not much has changed.”

Garrett said he does not back down from a challenge by teammates.

“I just haven’t lost,” he said.

Coach Sean McVay welcomes the team-building component of the competition.

“It’s always about when can you find those times to lock in but when can you do those things that organically occur to create a camaraderie and a connection that is something that only the players can really be able to do,” McVay said. “When you’re hearing laughs, I think that’s the sign of a good culture.”

Garrett played 37 of 62 defensive snaps against the Commanders and said he was “tired as hell” afterward.

After the Rams play the Cardinals, they will have what will essentially be a mini-bye before playing the Green Bay Packers on the night before Thanksgiving.

Garrett said the bye was coming at “a perfect time” for all players.

“Being able to get some extra practice myself, being on the field and being able to train and work on some things, get in my rhythm even without some games, I think will help us all in the long run,” he said.

item.title: Future Broncos: 3 Prospects to Watch in Week 11 of NCAA Football Season
item.description: Here are three collegiate prospects Broncos Country should watch in Week 11 of the NCAA Football Season.
item.content:encoded:
Welcome back to another installment of Future Broncos. Last week, I focused on a trio of defenders for Broncos Country to keep their eye on as the rest of the collegiate football season transpires. This week, I’ll switch gears and offer three players on offense since that side of the ball has been Denver’s biggest issue in 2026.

Earnest Green III — Offensive Tackle — Georgia

So far this season, I’ve offered my thoughts on a handful of offensive line prospects. Mizzou’s Cayden Green, Indiana’s Carter Smith, Minnesota’s Greg Johnson, and USC’s Elijah Paige. Based on the comments section, identifying more big guys in the offensive trenches is something you are all interested in.

Georgia fifth-year senior Earnest Green III has been on my radar for a while. Back in 2023, he was a fourteen-game starter for the Bulldogs at left tackle protecting future top pick Carson Beck. He continued to man down that position for nine games in 2024, but a lingering shoulder issue cost him a few games and slowed the promise he showed as a freshman.

Last season, Greene (6’4″, 320 pounds) flipped to right tackle while Monroe Freeling was manning the blindside. However, he started just nine games due to lingering back issues. Though he didn’t give up a sack in the over 800 offensive snaps he played in 2005.

Now healthy, Greene is back home where it all started on the left side of Georgia’s stalwart offensive line. The redshirt senior is poised to finish his collegiate career with over 40 starts and over 3,000 snaps between both tackle positions and having three different line coaches. That experience will pay off and mean a lot to NFL scouts and general managers who value experience and top-notch SEC pedigrees.

I’m a big fan of the depth he gets in his pass sets. I also like his ability to anchor and hold his own against strong power rushers. Moreover, I am impressed with his ability to get up field and take on blockers at the second level. It’ll be interesting to see how he measures [arm length] during the pre-draft circuit. There are some who believe his best football is inside at guard, but I think he can stick at tackle.

Last week’s performance versus Ole Miss earned him the Outland Trophy Player of the Week honors. To date, Greene has only given up four quarterback pressures on the season. The Broncos could use a tough and battle-tested player in their trenches next April, and I believe Greene (if medicals check out) has a shot at being a Day 2 selection. You can catch him in action this afternoon on ABC when the top-ranked Bulldogs host Mizzou.

Anthonie Knapp — Offensive Lineman — Notre Dame

For most of my Future Broncos installments, I’ve tried to focus on seniors whether it be fourth or fifth-year players. One particular reason is that NIL money has changed the NFL Draft landscape. Early declarations are basically half of what they used to be. In turn, that makes it a lot harder to find quality players to address needs.

However, a potential early round pick that may wind up declaring early if he keeps playing well is Notre Dame offensive lineman Anthonie Knapp. He manned down the left tackle position for the Fighting Irish for the first 27 games of his collegiate career. For his third season, the junior has kicked inside to guard.

That’s where many analysts have stated his best NFL potential might be. However, there are a handful of others who think a further kick inside to the pivot may be where he blossoms. Regardless, his versatility will be a big enhancer for his draft stock if he chooses to declare.

We all know Head Coach Sean Payton values experience and versatility when it comes to offensive lineman. This Golden Domer certainly fits the bill. By the end of this season, Knapp (6’5”, 305 pounds) will have logged well over 2,000 snaps and have three full seasons of starting experience.

While he could stand to put on some weight and muscle to handle the rigors of the pro game, his anchor is incredibly strong at this stage. In my opinion, he plays with NFL ready technique at the line of scrimmage. He has been an enforcer in the run game and a key reason for Notre Dame’s success on the ground this season. As a pass protector, Knapp has been credited with giving up just one sack in nearly three dozen starts.

Whether or not Knapp chooses to declare remains to be seen but given Denver’s long-term needs at multiple positions on the offensive line, he would be a quality prospect for them to consider. I believe he has a legitimate shot to be a Top 50 player easily if he decides to take his talents to the NFL. You can watch him in action when the third-ranked Fighting Irish host Boston College this afternoon.

DJ Vonnahme — Tight End — Iowa

Thus far in our Future Broncos installments, we have highlighted just two tight ends in the 2027 NFL Draft. Underclassmen Oregon’s Jamari Johnson and Virginia Tech’s Luke Reynolds. I have a strong feeling both of them will declare and will merit early consideration by NFL teams looking to upgrade the position.

This collegiate season, another underclassman from Iowa is making quite the statement this season—DJ Vonnahme. Over the years, the Hawkeyes have been a tight end producing factory under Kirk Ferentz. Players like George Kittle, Noah Fant, T.J. Hockensen, and Sam LaPorta all come to mind.

Vonnahme (6’4”, 241 pounds) appears to be next to follow in their footsteps. Appearing in twelve games as a redshirt freshman in 2025, Vonnahme logged five starts and was the Hawkeyes’ leading receiver with 29 catches, 434 yards, and 3 touchdowns. He popped onto the map of scouts last season with a dominant seven catch, 146-yard performance against Vanderbilt in last year’s ReliaQuest Bowl.

In eight games in 2026, Vonnahme sports 32 receptions for 314 yards and 3 touchdowns as well as one rushing touchdown. His yards per route ran (2.59) is amongst the highest in the nation. He has one of the best contested catch rates in the nation and can work multiple levels of the field.

While there is no doubting his upside and talent as a receiving threat at the next level, Vonnahme’s work as a blocker leaves a lot to be desired. It’s important to note he is only 20 years old and is a former quarterback that is still learning the nuances of the position. Getting better at blocking is something he can certainly get better at with more time.

Vonnahme is just a redshirt sophomore. With that in mind, a return back to Iowa seems quite likely. Though with this year’s class not having a clear-cut number one just yet, perhaps he goes pro if he gets good enough feedback in the pre-draft process. You can catch him in tonight when the sixteenth ranked Hawkeyes host Purdue tomorrow evening on NBC.

item.title: Amid a bittersweet winning streak, Rams look for revenge against Cardinals
item.description: The Rams have won three consecutive games, but it has come at a cost, with Puka Nacua the latest standout player injured ahead of their contest with the Cardinals.
item.content:encoded:
The Rams bounced back from an embarrassing, season-opening performance and a 2-4 start.

Myles Garrett returned to the lineup and dominated.

Coach Sean McVay’s team is now riding a three-game winning streak.

It took awhile, but the team that opened the season as the Super Bowl favorite is finally on a roll.

So why doesn’t it feel that way?

With receiver Puka Nacua the latest star to hit injured reserve, the Rams are anything but giddy heading into Sunday’s game against the Arizona Cardinals in Glendale, Ariz.

“It has been unique with the amount of different information that you’re dealing with and different injuries,” McVay said, “but we’re excited to have won those last three games.”

The Rams have not lost since Oct. 18, when Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur — the Rams’ former offensive coordinator — outcoached McVay in an 18-16 victory at SoFi Stadium. The Cardinals’ victory extended the LaFleur brothers’ record to 6-0 over McVay, who is 0-5 against Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur.

The Rams subsequently defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, the Chargers and the Washington Commanders.

But tight end Terrance Ferguson suffered a hamstring injury the day before the Rams departed to play the Commanders, and Nacua suffered a knee sprain and toe injury on the Rams’ final play of the 20-13 victory.

“There have been a lot of people in and out, [which] sometimes takes that major joy out of a win sometimes,” quarterback Matthew Stafford said when asked about the team’s mood. “You’re like, ‘Man, we just won, but we lost Puka for a little bit of time,’ or we lost ‘Ferg.’ ...

“That’s part of it. Then I think, frankly, there are opportunities for us to play better a little bit as well.”

The Rams, who led the NFL in offense and scoring last season, are tied for fourth in yards, averaging 379.8, and 13th in points (23.8).

The defense is giving up 302.4 yards and 20.1 points per game, which ranks fifth and eighth, respectively.

Special teams problems that plagued the Rams in the first seven games appear to be resolved for now.

Last season, after Davante Adams suffered a hamstring injury, McVay masterfully pivoted to an attack relying heavily on multiple tight ends.

With Nacua and Adams out, will McVay make another significant shift? Perhaps a two-back set?

“I think you explore everything,” McVay said.

Running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum said they can carry a heavier load and also augment a depleted receiver corps that now includes Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, Brennan Presley and rookie CJ Daniels.

“Kyren and I prepare for anything,” Corum said. “Our mindset, whether we run a lot or don’t, we’re ready for whatever coach feels is best for this team.”

Williams said he attended college recruiting camps as a slot receiver. So if McVay asked him to split out wide?

“I’m fine with it,” he said. “I’ll do anything with a smile on my face, especially that.”

Read more:With NFL's toughest schedule looming, Rams quiet at trade deadline as rivals make deals

The last time they played the Cardinals, the Rams were without left tackle Alaric Jackson, who had been suspended for punching a Buffalo Bills player after a defeat. item.title: Saints sent Jordyn Tyson to renowned hamstring specialist at University of Wisconsin
item.description: In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr.
item.content:encoded:
In 2021, the NFL awarded a $4 million grant to Dr. Bryan Heiderscheit and his team at the University of Wisconsin to research new ways to prevent and treat hamstring injuries. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson may benefit from that research.

Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports that the Saints sent Tyson on two separate visits to the University of Wisconsin to be evaluated by Dr. Heiderscheit and his team.

Hamstring injuries have been a major problem for Tyson, who was out for three months with a hamstring injury before finally making his NFL debut last week. Tyson also missed time at Arizona State last year because of a hamstring injury, and he didn't run at either Arizona State's Pro Day or the NFL Scouting Combine because of his hamstring.

But there's hope for Tyson after his evaluations in Wisconsin. Heiderscheit was able to identify a weakness with Tyson's hamstring that he thinks can be strengthened with a specific workout regimen that Tyson has been following.

Heiderscheit previously worked with Packers wide receiver Christian Watson and helped him recover from hamstring injuries, and it worked: Watson has started every game this season and in nine games already has career-highs with 49 catches for 879 yards, and he's leading the NFL with an average of 17.9 yards per catch.

That's the kind of player the Saints think Tyson can be, if he can stay healthy. Heiderscheit's treatment may be the key to Tyson staying healthy.

item.title: Steelers-Bengals rematch might have the highest stakes of NFL season so far
item.description: Both teams will likely be favored in most of their remaining games of 2026, which could make it difficult for the loser to catch the winner.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals may well decide the AFC North with their Sunday Night Football rematch Nov. 16. 

It feels quite early to be making such a bold declaration. Fully nine weeks of action remain starting with NFL Week 10 this week, and they could include plenty of twists and turns that we don’t anticipate right now. 

On paper, however, soft schedules could make it difficult for the loser of this primetime matchup to make up ground on the other over the course of the next couple of months. 

Required reading: Steelers' Omar Khan stands pat at trade deadline, makes no major moves

Both are 6-2 currently, and one will leave the weekend with a full one-game lead. If the Steelers win, they’ll also own the head-to-head tiebreaker thanks to their 30-27 victory when these teams first met Sept. 27 at Acrisure Stadium.

Steelers fans originally feared another second-half meatgrinder when dates were announced back in May. Opponents including the Philadelphia Eagles, Denver Broncos, Houston Texans, Jacksonville Jaguars and Carolina Panthers all made the playoffs last season. 

The slate also includes both matchups with the division rival Baltimore Ravens, who pushed the Steelers to the final play of the final game of the regular season to decide which team would represent the North in the 2025 playoffs. 

Things look far more manageable now. Of those six opponents, only the Jaguars and Broncos currently have winning records, and the Steelers play only one of the two on the road. They’ll travel to face Jacksonville on Monday Night Football on Dec. 14. 

The Eagles (2-7), Texans (3-5) and Panthers (3-5) have been among the league’s worst teams through nine weeks. The Ravens (4-5) aren’t quite as bad, but are navigating injuries to former MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson and his backup Tyler Huntley. 

Throw in a Week 17 visit to the 1-7 Tennessee Titans on Jan. 3 and it’s reasonable to expect the Steelers will be favored in most of their games the rest of the way. 

The road is only slightly tougher for the Bengals. Of their remaining opponents, only the Panthers were a 2025 playoff team. 

The Washington Commanders (2-5-1), New Orleans Saints (3-5) and Indianapolis Colts (2-7) all have losing records as well. And one matchup remains against those hobbled Ravens on New Year’s Eve. 

Cincinnati will face three teams with a winning record compared to Pittsburgh’s two. Both division matchups with the 5-3 Cleveland Browns remain, and a Dec. 13 home game against Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs could be tricky. 

Still, the Bengals would have plenty of reason to feel confident if they could pull out a win against the Steelers in a game in which they’re currently favored by 3.5 points, per BetMGM.  That reality puts a premium on winning for both sides. 

Bigger picture, neither team looks like it’s in a ton of danger of missing the playoffs. Eight AFC teams currently have winning records, and seven can make the playoffs. Most of those contenders have tougher remaining schedules, so both the Steelers and Bengals would need to fumble badly to miss the bracket. 

The winner of the North gets a coveted home playoff game, though. And that’s of particular importance to the Steelers. 

They’ve not won a postseason game since 2016, and they’re just 2-6 in playoff road games since their Super Bowl loss to the Green Bay Packers at the end of the 2010 season.

The stakes are therefore fairly high for a game this early in the season. 

The Bengals prevailed when these teams last met in Cincinnati early last season. Backup quarterback Joe Flacco sliced and diced the Steelers’ secondary for 342 yards and three touchdowns in what became a 33-31 victory Oct. 16. 

Otherwise, the Steelers have won in three of their past four visits to Paycor Stadium. The teams have split their 12 meetings, 6-6, since star Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow broke into the league in 2020.

Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know this weekend.

The Giants will be rooting hard for the 49ers this weekend. That’s because if the Cowboys somehow beat San Francisco, they’ll move closer to the Giants in the NFC East race.

The Giants are 5-3-1 after Thursday night’s 24-21 gut-punch loss to the Commanders. Coach John Harbaugh’s team remains alone atop the division, ahead of the 4-5 Cowboys and 3-5-1 Commanders (who now have the head-to-head tiebreaker edge over the Giants).

On to the next one

Why J.J. McCarthy kept chucking ball downfield before game-sealing interception in Giants’ crushing loss | New York Post

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy certainly shouldn’t shoulder all the blame, but an interception with 25 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter sealed the loss and gave the Commanders the tiebreaker over the Giants after the two teams tied in Week 5. Despite being at the Washington 48-yard line with 40 seconds remaining and needing only a field goal, McCarthy threw deep on his final two passes. The first fell to the turf for an incomplete pass, and the second was intended for Malik Nabers but instead landed in Rasul Douglas’ arms to end the Giants’ comeback attempt.

“My thought process was pop it up to my playmakers, have them go make a play,” McCarthy said.

What we saw as NY Giants fail to seal the deal against Commanders | The Record

For the first time all season, the New York Giants failed to deliver with the lead in the fourth quarter and the game on the line.

Jayden Daniels’ third touchdown pass, this one to Stefon Diggs, as two Giants defenders ran into each other with 57 seconds remaining allowed Washington to snap Big Blue’s two-game winning streak with a 24-21 victory at MetLife Stadium.

Cam Skattebo scores twice after Giants’ quiet trade deadline, but wonders if he could’ve done more in loss to Commanders | New York Daily News

But after the Giants’ offense stagnated down the stretch of a 24-21 loss — with Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy both getting stopped on third-down QB keepers — Skattebo was left wondering if he could have done more. “It sucks, and I think part of it is I put myself in a situation last time we played these guys that kind of killed the trust in Coach [John Harbaugh] maybe a little bit, of giving up the ball last time,” Skattebo said. “And maybe he didn’t want to give me the ball again. I don’t know. I’m not gonna say that was something that he was thinking, but I would think that as well.”

Skattebo followed with runs of five and two yards, setting up a crucial 3rd and 3. But on a designed QB run, McCarthy was tackled by Sonny Styles behind the line of scrimmage, prompting another Giants punt. Asked if he felt he could have led the Giants into field-goal range had he gotten the ball, Skattebo replied, “I can’t say that. Do I think that? Yeah, but I can’t say that, because it could’ve been any situation at any time.”

New York Giants slam ‘corny’ DPI penalty called on Deonte Banks | USAToday.com

“This league is funny, bro,” said Safety Tyler Nubin. “This league is funny. There’s really nothing you can do about it, man. When you’re in trail position, nine times out of 10, they’re going to call that PI. That’s just how the league is. Just got to weather it.”

“I’m going to be honest, and I ain’t going to say nothing that gets me fined,” Safety Jason Pinnock said. “But it’s getting to a point now where [offensive coordinators] are taking advantage of it. They’re not calling real plays. They’re going four wide, and they’re throwing that junk outside. And it looks like these receivers literally have techniques to get PIs. They’re grabbing the back of DBs’ necks. It’s almost like it’s becoming a technique.”

The window that J.J. McCarthy put this in….

2026 NFL midseason award rankings: MVP picks, top rookies, OPOY, DPOY, coaches | ESPN.com

Defensive Rookie of the Year. 1. Arvell Reese, LB/Edge, New York Giants. Picking between Bailey and Reese is unfair. I leaned Reese if only because he has been two impactful players in one this season. As an off-ball linebacker, Reese has been all over the place for a Giants team that has been better against the run this season, even after trading Dexter Lawrence II. Reese has made tackles on 15.3% of his snaps, the eighth-highest rate in the league. He has given up an 81.3 passer rating in coverage, a very credible number for a veteran linebacker, let alone a rookie just getting his feet wet at this level.

And then there’s Reese’s side quest as a devastating force on blitzes. Despite rushing the quarterback only about 11 times per game, Reese already has 4.5 sacks and 14 pressures. His 10.2% quick pressure rate would be the second-best mark in the NFL if he qualified. And the average Reese pressure comes after 2.44 seconds, the fifth fastest among players with 10 pressures or more.

NFL midseason superlatives and lessons: Josh Allen for MVP, all-in moves, dashed hopes | The Athletic

Defensive rookie of the year – LB Arvell Reese, New York Giants. The No. 5 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has racked up 4.5 sacks, eight tackles for loss, 49 solo tackles (68 total), a forced fumble and an interception for the surprising Giants.

Coach of the Year — John Harbaugh, New York Giants. Ben Johnson continues to lead an impressive Chicago Bears team, and Kyle Shanahan’s 49ers rank among the Super Bowl favorites. But with the Giants unexpectedly leading their division and contending for their first playoff berth since the 2022 season — with a backup quarterback, no less — Harbaugh gets the nod.

2026 NFL DROY Odds: Which New York Rookie Has The Edge? | FOX Sports

 Arvell Reese has jumped David Bailey on the odds board and sits at +100 after Week 9. The Giants rookie was drafted with the fifth pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, and so far, he’s exceeding those expectations. Through nine weeks, Reese is second in the entire NFL in solo tackles (49) and leads the Giants’ defense in total tackles as a rookie. Reese joined Nick Bosa (2019) as the only players in the last 25 seasons with at least four sacks, an interception, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery in their first eight career games. It looks like the G-Men have finally found a guy they can build their defense around for the next decade.

NFL midseason awards: The good, the bad and the Dallas Cowboys | Yahoo! Sports

The ‘Chicken Salad from Chicken S**t’ Award: New York Giants. Boy, the Giants were feeling fine after their Week 1 win over Dallas. And just as quickly, hopes deflated when Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury in Week 2. But somehow, the Giants have cobbled together win after win, using quarterback after quarterback, and suddenly they’re dangerous. Granted, it’s a “is that stray dog going to beg for food or bite my face?” kind of dangerous, but it’s better than nothing.

item.title: Drew Mestemaker is one win away from crashing the Heisman race
item.description: Drew Mestemaker can lead Oklahoma State to an upset win over Texas Tech in Week 11. He can also claim more than just a win with a big game.
item.content:encoded:
Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker has already led one upset over a ranked team at home this season. He's looking to do it again against Texas Tech on Saturday, Nov. 14, although this time he could potentially claim even more than just a win.

Mestemaker, who ranks second nationally with 2,962 passing yards and first nationally with 29 passing touchdowns this season, is near the top of not only NFL draft boards, but also the Heisman Trophy race. There will be lots of eyes on Mestemaker and Oklahoma State in Week 11, especially with it being a night game against a top opponent with Big 12 implications on the line.

Expert picks for every Top 25 game: College football Week 11 predictions

Mestemaker has done it all for the Cowboys and first-year coach Eric Morris this season, leading the program to one of the best turnarounds in college football after winning only one game in 2025. It's a big reason he's expected to be the first quarterback off the board in the 2027 NFL Draft, even if he hasn't declared yet.

The former walk-on from North Texas who never started a game at quarterback in high school isn't thinking about his draft status or what's to come, though, despite a potential win over Texas Tech placing him in the elite tier of Heisman candidates this season.

"No," Mestemaker said when asked if he's thought of the NFL Draft yet. "I think this team is special and this season is special, honestly, and there’s no point in thinking about that after because there’s nothing I can do about it right now."

The 6-3 quarterback led the country in passing yards (4,379) as a first-year starter last season at North Texas, nearly leading the Mean Green to the College Football Playoff after scoring 39 total touchdowns. Mestemaker and his two top weapons — running back Caleb Hawkins and receiver Wyatt Young — then followed Morris to Oklahoma State, where the trio has emerged as three of the best offensive players in the Big 12 this season.

Mestemaker garnered some hype as a future top-tier prospect after his first season as a starting quarterback since middle school at North Texas last season, but questions still remained. His play against Power Four opponents — including his 426 total yards with three touchdowns in a 39-31 win over Oregon earlier this season — eased those questions, with 17 of 25 anonymous scouts in a recent poll by ESPN favoring Mestemaker as the top quarterback in the upcoming NFL draft.

Mestemaker isn't talking about the NFL Draft anytime soon, a stance that Morris said his other NFL quarterbacks he has coached like Patrick Mahomes and Cam Ward also took in college.

"We already had the discussion we’re not going to talk about this stuff until the end of the season," Morris said. "I think that’s right for everybody in this program. He owes that to our team. I owe that to this team. So, we’ll continue going and chopping this wood every single day and at the end of the year just sit down and have a discussion with him and his mom and figure out what’s best for the kid and his future.

"This isn’t the first time I’ve had that conversation and nor will it be the last time I have that conversation."

Texas Tech is coming off back-to-back one-score wins over Arizona and West Virginia, with its offense taking a step forward after changing to Tommy Castellanos at quarterback. Mestemaker and Oklahoma State's offense has had to dig its poor defense out of numerous holes this season, setting up for a potential back-and-forth game on Saturday night.

There's a lot on the line for Mestemaker against the Red Raiders, with Oklahoma State staying in the Big 12 championship game race.

Have a big performance and a Heisman could be within his grasp, too.

"I just love playing football and this week is a dream football game (vs. Texas Tech) you dream about playing and so my close circle and my friends and family we don’t talk about that," Mestemaker said. "There might be a decision after the season to make, but that’s an after the season decision to make."

Drew Mestemaker NFL mock draft projection

Here's a look at where Mestemaker's latest projections for the 2027 NFL Draft:

  • USA TODAY: No. 4 overall to the Philadelphia Eagles
  • The Athletic: No. 3 overall to the Miami Dolphins
  • ESPN: No. 2 overall to Miami Dolphins

Drew Mestemaker stats

  • 2024 (North Texas): 30-of-46 passing (65.2%) for 462 yards with two touchdowns to two interceptions; 14 carries for 87 yards with a touchdown
  • 2025 (North Texas): 319-of-463 passing (68.9%) for 4,379 yards with 34 touchdowns to nine interceptions; 57 carries for 89 yards with five touchdowns
  • 2026 (Oklahoma State): 206-of-309 passing (66.7%) for 2,962 yards with 29 touchdowns to eight interceptions; 36 carries for 177 yards with three touchdowns

item.title: Joe Burrow can join Peyton Manning as only QBs with 4 total TDs in 5 straight games
item.description: A big game from Burrow on Sunday night would put him in some very exclusive company in NFL history.
item.content:encoded:
Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow has been racking up touchdowns recently, and if he continues to do it on Sunday night against the Steelers, he'll join some very exclusive company in NFL history.

Burrow has had at least four touchdowns, combined rushing and passing, in each of the last four games. If Burrow has another four-touchdown game on Sunday night, he will join Peyton Manning as the only quarterbacks in NFL history with at least four combined passing and rushing touchdowns in five consecutive games.

Burrow's last four games:
Three touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 34-17 win over the Falcons.
Five touchdown passes and one touchdown run in a 43-36 win over the Titans.
Four touchdown passes in a 35-13 win over the Ravens.
Four touchdown passes in a 31-24 win over the Dolphins.

Manning became the first quarterback to have five straight games with four touchdowns in Weeks 8-12 of 2004 with the Colts, when he had a six-touchdown game, two five-touchdown games and two four-touchdown games. (All of Manning's touchdowns were passing, not rushing.) Manning was named NFL MVP that season.

And Burrow is an MVP candidate with the way he's playing now. A win over the Steelers on Sunday night would put the Bengals in first place in the AFC North, and a big game with those big stakes would give a big boost to Burrow's MVP chances.

item.description: Your daily San Francisco 49ers news for Saturday, November 14th, 2026
item.content:encoded:
49ers-Cowboys preview: Christian McCaffrey and the Niners should run wild
“When you watch them, the issues stem from getting moved at the point of attack. Ball carriers aren’t getting touched until they cross the line of scrimmage. The eye test matches the stats: Dallas allows the second-most yards before contact per carry this season, at 1.78 yards. They get moved, easily, despite having played only two offenses in the top-15 in rushing success rate.

The 49ers are running more and more inside the tackles. They’re running inside zone at a 19.1% clip, a slight increase from a year ago. This game sets up well for the Niners to keep attacking the Cowboys’ A and B gaps.

Kyle Shanahan had to be grinning as he watched the 36-play reel of the Cowboys’ defense defending —a term used loosely—inside zone. They allowed 8.08 yards per carry. Seven of those 36 plays went for double digits. They allowed a 58.3% success rate.

You could build the case that the 49ers aren’t running inside enough this season. Christian McCaffrey had two 11-yard runs on inside zone last week. McCaffrey has 24 inside zone carries this year and averages 5.04 yards per carry, with a 62.5% success rate….Rookie Caleb Downs is the player the Niners could find success against. He’s primarily played nickel. Against the Texans, Packers, and Cardinals, Downs allowed all 9 of his targets to be completed for 147 yards.

Heading into Week 9, Downs had allowed a 90.5% completion percentage, which was the third-highest among slot cornerbacks this season. He has one pass breakup. Dallas tried to align him closer to the line of scrimmage, almost like a pseudo-linebacker in coverage against Arizona. He played linebacker 32.1% of the time against the Cardinals.…Downs is not a big player. He’s 5’11”, 206 pounds, but has a 10th percentile arm length. That shows up in contested situations when he can’t make plays on the ball.”

If it gets picked, I’m gonna come out and do it again because they trust me.’ And that’s the only way we win is by throwing these balls on time, throwing to these spots, and trusting it.’ …

item.title: Milton Williams takes action to address Patriots’ penalty problem
item.description: The Patriots have been flagged for seven infractions the last two weeks.
item.content:encoded:
Pre-snap penalties have been a major problem for the New England Patriots defense this season. 

Defensive tackle Milton Williams has had enough.

“I put in fines this week,” the defensive tackle revealed Friday “$1,000 fine for whoever jumps offsides.”

Williams has been guilty of the infraction himself, getting flagged twice in the first three weeks of the season and again in Week 7. Those miscues helped inspire the new system.

“I had a couple early in the season, and I feel like we talked about it, but is not enough consequences that come with it other than hurting the team,” Williams said. “So [if] it hurt your pockets, maybe you’ll think about it a little more.”

The penalties have become more prevalent in recent weeks, with the Patriots defense flagged for seven infractions over the last two games. On the season, New England leads the league in encroachment penalties (4), ranks fourth in neutral zone infractions (5) and is tied for the eighth-most defensive offsides penalties (3).

Williams said cleaning up those small details will be an important part of the defense’s effort to bounce back after allowing a season-high 45 points to the Green Bay Packers last week.

“It’s on us to be ready to go, be ready for the hard count, we’ve been jumping offsides. We’ve got to be ready for that stuff going into every game,” Williams said. “It’s costing us. We want to get teams in third and five-plus situations so we can go out there and rush. Jumping offsides is just giving them third and short, so we can’t go rush the passer.”

According to Williams, any fines collected will go toward members of the team’s training staff or custodians in the building.

“We’ll take care of somebody in the building. They’ll have a pretty good lunch on us, if we can’t do what we’re supposed to do,” he said.

Since signing a four-year, $104 million contract with the Patriots last offseason, Williams has established himself as one of the team’s leaders. Craig Woodson was not yet aware of the fine system from his safety position, but he praised Williams for holding his teammates accountable.

“I mean, that’s a leader right there,” Woodson said. “That’s something that we got to make sure that we can’t give them free yards. So, for him to do that, that’s a leader.”
